title: Autofluorescence-driven isolation of human peripheral blood eosinophils
author: Weihrauch, Gray, et al.
materials: Giemsa’s azure eosin methylene blue solution

Timing: 30 min
2.Start and initialize all devices and precool the centrifuges and MACSQuant Tyto to 4°C.3.Prepare the reagents as listed in materials and equipment.

steps.title: Prepare equipment and reagents
steps.instruction: Start and initialize all devices, precool centrifuges and the MACSQuant Tyto to 4 °C. Prepare staining buffer by dissolving one tablet (pH 7.2) in 1 L ultrapure water on a magnetic stirrer and store at 4 °C for up to 3 months. Prepare Giemsa staining solution by mixing 1 mL Giemsa’s azure eosin methylene blue solution with 19 mL staining buffer (final 1:20 dilution) and let stand 10 min before use.

substeps.instruction: Initialize devices and set temperature to 4 °C
Prepare staining buffer (1 tablet in 1 L water, pH 7.2)
Store staining buffer at 4 °C (≤3 months)
Prepare Giemsa solution (1 mL Giemsa stock + 19 mL buffer, 1:20)
Let Giemsa solution sit 10 min before use

steps.title: Lyse red blood cells
steps.instruction: Transfer 3–5 mL EDTA‑blood into a 50 mL conical tube, add lysis buffer up to 50 mL, vortex 5 s, incubate at 19–22 °C for 7 min, centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, discard all supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL PBS + 1 % BSA and keep on ice.

steps.title: Determine eosinophil count and rate
steps.instruction: Dilute 10 µL of the cell suspension with 40 µL PBS, run on a Beckman Cytoflex S (or equivalent) using the 405/450 nm and 405/525 nm channels, set the eosinophil autofluorescence gate according to Figure 1, record percentage and total cell count and calculate the required dilution for Tyto Running Buffer. Adjust settings if a different flow cytometer is used.

steps.title: Prime and load sorting cartridge
steps.instruction: Place the cartridge on the MACSQuant Tyto priming fixture aligning the feet, attach a syringe (plunger removed) to the intake chamber, add 300 µL PBS + 1 % BSA and gently push the plunger until PBS appears in the positive collection chamber, stop. Close the pressure inlet O‑ring, continue pushing until PBS appears in the negative collection chamber, stop and remove the syringe. Keep the cartridge on ice. Dilute the 1 mL cell suspension in the calculated volume of Tyto Running Buffer to a maximum of 2.1 × 10⁶ total cells / mL with an eosinophil rate of 0.8–8.2 % (max sorting volume 10 mL, eosinophil count ≤1 × 10⁶ cells / mL). Attach a new syringe (plunger removed), place a 20 µm pre‑separation filter on it, filter the entire suspension (apply gentle air pressure or pre‑wet filter if needed), remove the filter, insert the plunger and transfer the suspension into the input chamber, then remove the syringe and close the intake.

substeps.instruction: Prime cartridge on fixture
Add PBS + 1 % BSA and push plunger to fill positive chamber
Close pressure inlet, push to fill negative chamber
Remove syringe, keep cartridge on ice
Dilute cell suspension in Tyto Running Buffer (≤2.1 × 10⁶ cells/mL, eosinophil 0.8–8.2 %)
Attach syringe with 20 µm filter, filter suspension
Remove filter, insert plunger, transfer suspension to input chamber
Close intake chamber

steps.title: Sort eosinophils on MACSQuant Tyto
steps.instruction: Scan the cartridge 2‑D barcode, insert cartridge with input chamber facing the user (propeller should spin). In the UI select cartridge type, enter sample name and total sorting volume. Configure live dot plot with CFP/VioBlue‑H on Y‑axis and VioGreen‑H on X‑axis, start cell flow (Play), set a gate on the eosinophil population per Figure 3 and assign it as the sorting gate, then start sorting (Sort). Keep abortion rate below 1 %; if higher, dilute the suspension further. Stop sorting when the desired number of eosinophils is collected. Open the sort chamber, transfer sorted cells to a 1.5 mL tube with a gel‑loading tip, measure the exact volume. Wash the sort chamber twice with 100 µL PBS, collect washes, keep cells on ice. Cells are now ready for downstream assays.

substeps.instruction: Scan cartridge barcode
Insert cartridge correctly
Select cartridge type and input sample details
Configure live dot plot (CFP/VioBlue‑H vs VioGreen‑H)
Start cell flow
Set eosinophil gate (Figure 3)
Start sorting
Monitor abortion rate (<1 %)
Stop sort when target reached
Collect sorted eosinophils into tube, record volume
Wash sort chamber twice with 100 µL PBS
Keep cells on ice

steps.title: Assess purity and viability by flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Transfer the volume containing 50 000 sorted eosinophils to a microcentrifuge tube, centrifuge 7 min at 350 × g, 4 °C, discard supernatant carefully, resuspend pellet in 100 µL PBS and mix. Split 50 µL into two 1.5 mL tubes. Add 1 µL PC7‑conjugated anti‑Siglec‑8 to one tube and mix; add 1 µL 7‑AAD to the other tube and mix (include an FMO control without staining). Incubate both tubes 10 min in the dark at 19–22 °C, then add 200 µL PBS to each, mix, and analyse PC7 (Siglec‑8) and PC5.5 (7‑AAD) fluorescence on a flow cytometer.

steps.title: Prepare cytospins for Giemsa staining
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 50 000 purified eosinophils onto a microscopy slide for 7 min at 350 × g, resuspend pellet in 50 µL PBS. Assemble cytospin: place filter card between slide and sample chamber aligning the hole with the funnel, secure with a cytoclip, add 50 µL cell suspension to the funnel, centrifuge 5 min at 500 × g, 19–22 °C. Remove chambers, let slides dry 10 min (or store at –20 °C). Fix slides by immersing in methanol for 5 min in a fume hood, then air‑dry.

steps.title: Giemsa stain cytospins
steps.instruction: Draw a hydrophobic barrier around the eosinophil spot with a pen and briefly air‑dry. Place slide flat, pipette 200 µL diluted Giemsa staining solution onto the spot (ensure a domed drop that does not overflow). Incubate 20 min at 19–22 °C, wash twice in staining buffer for 1 min each, air‑dry, add 50 µL mounting medium, cover with a coverslip, and let dry under the fume hood before microscopy.

steps.title: Assess CD16 expression by flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 50 000 sorted eosinophils 7 min at 350 × g, 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 50 µL PBS. Add 1.5 µL CD16 antibody and mix (optional: also stain with Siglec‑8 using appropriate fluorophore). Incubate 10 min in the dark at 19–22 °C, then dilute with 200 µL PBS, mix, and analyse CD16 (and optional Siglec‑8) fluorescence. Include an FMO control (unstained) to set the CD16‑negative gate. Optional: sort CD16‑ or CD16+ eosinophils in a separate run (not validated).
